chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Yahya ibn Hajjaj, from Khalid ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the sailor (merchant/transporter): I entrust him with food, then I take it from him and it is found to be deficient. He said, 'If he is trustworthy, do not make him liable for compensation (guarantee the deficiency).'

key_terms.تُضَمِّنْهُ: Make him liable/guarantee him liable for compensation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on holding a trustworthy transporter liable for missing goods?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of *al-amanah* (trustworthiness) in maritime commerce, establishing that a reliable carrier is not automatically liable for natural losses or minor deficiencies unless explicitly guaranteed. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on distinguishing between negligence and inherent wear-and-tear in commercial contracts, reinforcing the ethical expectation of trust in business dealings. The ruling underscores the importance of verifying the carrier's integrity before entrusting valuable goods, a key consideration in Islamic commercial law.
